_comment: Curated box interiors — the launch set of the game-box dimension KB (issue #154,
roadmap §0.5, PRD F4). Read by pythonsrc/organizer/box_kb.py; every rule stated
here is enforced there, at load, so this file cannot acquire a bad row quietly.
WHY A COMMITTED FILE AND NOT A TABLE. This is curation, reviewed in a diff, exactly
like data/ip_blocklist.json. A table would be a migration, the DDL is generated from
pythonsrc/telemetry/db.py and never hand-edited, and there is no write path that
would ever add a row at runtime — a measurement arrives in a pull request or it is
not a measurement anybody reviewed.
PROVENANCE IS PER VALUE. Each axis carries its own basis, source, capture date and
the units it was captured in. `source` is required and `basis` is one of spec /
measured / derived — the vocabulary of docs/dimension-kb-research.md §0. Its fourth
word, `folk` (a rule of thumb), is not accepted: a rule of thumb about box walls is
not a measurement of a box. A `derived` value must carry a `note` naming what it was
derived from, because inferring an interior from an exterior without saying so in
the data is the one thing this KB may not do.
`captured_on` is the date THIS PROJECT took the number off that source. It is not
the date the source measured it — nobody knows that, and claiming to would be the
fabrication the KB exists to refuse. All three launch entries carry 2026-08-31, the
research date in the header of docs/dimension-kb-research.md, because that document
is where they were transcribed from.
THERE IS NO BOARDGAMEGEEK CLIENT AND THERE MUST NOT BE ONE. BGG carries EXTERNAL box
dimensions only, user-entered, in inches, and its API is registration-gated under a
commercial licence (issue #154 §0.4; research §7). A BGG forum thread in which a
person reports measuring their own copy is a citation like any other and is used
below; the API is not touched, here or anywhere in the tree.
WHY THREE. Small and defensible beats broad and unsourced. Three is what this
repository can source today: every number below is transcribed from a row of
docs/dimension-kb-research.md that already names where it came from. Refused, with
the reason, so they are not rediscovered as omissions:
- Printables 245516 Commander box, internal 71 × 76 × 97 (research §3). The row is
marked unverified — it came from search snippets because the page is
Cloudflare-gated — and §8 says re-verify it manually before shipping it. Nobody
has. It joins when somebody opens the page.
- Every BGG box-dimension row. External only, and in inches somebody typed.
- Anything a wall thickness would have to be guessed for. Deriving an interior from
an exterior is supported by the schema (`basis: derived` plus a note), and no
entry here does it, because no source in this repository states the wall.
`version` is the CONTENT version, bumped whenever any entry's numbers, sources or
ids change; the SCHEMA version is the `.v1` in the filename. A spec built against an
entry records both the id and this version (`spec.box`), so a corrected measurement
never silently reinterprets a design that was built before it.
tests/test_game_box_kb.py pins this version beside a digest of the entries, so
editing a number without bumping the version fails the suite.

boxes.name: Wingspan
boxes.note: Base game box. The one publisher's board-game box this repository can source an interior for; the insert archetype's reference case.

width.note: Community caliper measurement of one copy, reported on the thread; transcribed via docs/dimension-kb-research.md §7. Boxes flare and vary ±1–2 mm between copies, which is what constraints.fit_margin_mm is for.

depth.note: Same thread; the footprint is square, so width and depth are the same measurement reported once.

height.note: Interior depth to the underside of the lid, as reported.

boxes.name: Ultimate Guard Boulder 100+
boxes.note: The commercial reference a snug deck box is judged against in docs/dimension-kb-research.md §3. Width is the stack direction; depth and height are the sleeved card's own 67 × 92 mm envelope plus clearance.

width.note: The manufacturer states the figure approximately (≈68,5); treat it as ±0,5 mm, which is inside what fit_margin_mm already absorbs.

depth.note: Approximate, as above. 0,5 mm over the 67 mm double-sleeved envelope measured in research §3.

height.note: Approximate, as above. 1 mm over the 92 mm double-sleeved envelope.

boxes.name: DeckSmith Commander box
boxes.note: The second commercial reference in docs/dimension-kb-research.md §3, and the roomier of the two: 8 mm more stack room than the Boulder for the same card envelope.

width.note: Stack direction. The manufacturer's stated internal dimension.

depth.note: 1 mm over the 67 mm double-sleeved envelope measured in research §3.

height.note: 6 mm over the 92 mm double-sleeved envelope; the card sits proud enough to grip.
